title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates the product overview, high-level PRD, prioritized requirements, design specifications, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for Redwood Inference's Unified Inference product. The goal is to provide a single-source reference for PMs, Eng, SRE, and GTM to align on scope, milestones, and launch activities.

Key product value proposition:
- Provide a unified runtime and developer experience for serving LLM workloads across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Optimize for production economics: predictable latency SLOs, lower per-token cost via batching, caching, and quantization guidance, and reliable fallbacks.
- Expose clear operational controls and observability to integrate into customers' existing platforms.

Goals (OKRs alignment):
- O1: Reduce median 95th-percentile inference latency by 15% for common production workloads by Q3 2026.
- O2: Decrease average per-token cost by 20% for enterprise workloads through Optimize recommendations and quantization profiles by Q4 2026.
- O3: Increase self-serve adoption of Dedicated reservations by 30% YoY through better packaging and onboarding flows.

Success metrics (product & launch):
- Latency: P95 <= configured SLO (default 250ms for small models, 600ms for large models).
- Cost: Per-token execution cost reduction (measured by Redwood billing) relative to baseline.
- Adoption: Number of teams using model-routing and cost-aware fallback policies.
- Reliability: >= 99.9% availability for Hosted APIs (customer-facing SLA targets defined in contracts for Dedicated).
- NPS / CSAT for early access customers >= 8/10 post-onboarding.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: Product engineers, platform engineers, SRE, ML engineers integrating inference into production services.
- Secondary: GTM, solutions, and partner engineers evaluating pricing and packaging.
- Out of scope: New model research (model training) and non-inference model lifecycle activities.

PRD Summary (high level):
- Minimum Viable Product (MVP):
  - Unified API endpoints for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking with consistent semantics across deployment modes.
  - Model catalog that surface latency and cost profiles per model variant.
  - Basic routing rules (region, latency, tier) and automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity constrained.
  - Redwood Optimize suggestions: batching, caching, and single-click quantization recommendations in Console.

- Targeted Capabilities (post-MVP):
  - Per-route kernel selection and sequence-length aware compilation.
  - Advanced rollout controls: canary + traffic-shift A/B with automated rollback on quality regressions.
  - Private deployment: hardened installer for on-prem and VPC with KMS/HSM integrations.

Requirements (MUST / SHOULD / MAY):
- MUST: Unified REST/SDK interface with feature parity for core ops (generate, chat, embeddings).
- MUST: Model catalog with verified perf profile metadata: model_name, token_throughput, p50/p95 latency, memory_footprint, quantization_supported (true/false).
- MUST: Developer console UI showing per-route latency/cost breakdown and a "recommendations" panel powered by Redwood Optimize.
- MUST: Routing policy engine that supports predicate rules (region, model, latency threshold, customer_tier) and a compatible-fallback chain.
- MUST: Observability hooks: tracing headers, per-token cost attribution, error categorization.
- SHOULD: Default batching parameters tuned per-model automatically with override per-route.
- SHOULD: Built-in QA/regression checks triggered during rollouts using saved prompt-sets and evals.
- MAY: Pre-built connectors for common data sources (S3, GCS) for prompt/context retrieval.

Acceptance criteria:
- API compatibility tests pass with sample workloads (text, chat, embeddings).
- Red-team load tests demonstrate target throughput and P95 latency under representative distributions.
- Console: Recommendations UI surfaces at least 3 actionable items for 80% of customer workloads in beta.

Design Specifications (high-level):
1) API and wire semantics:
- Endpoints: POST /v1/generate, POST /v1/chat, POST /v1/embeddings, POST /v1/rerank.
- Request envelope includes: model, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop, routing_hint, client_request_id.
- Streaming supported via chunked transfer and event-based SDKs.
- Example request (JSON):
  {
    "model": "redwood/unified-7b",
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "temperature": 0.2,
    "routing_hint": "low-latency"
  }

2) Model catalog metadata (table):
| field | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| model_name | string | canonical model id |
| variant | string | e.g., fp16, int8-qat |
| p50_latency_ms | string | median token latency (ms) |
| p95_latency_ms | string | 95th-percentile latency (ms) |
| throughput_tokens_per_sec | string | tokens/sec on representative GPU |
| quantization_supported | string | true/false |

3) Routing and fallback design:
- Routing engine evaluates ordered policies; first-matching policy binds request. Policies can be static or dynamic (SLO-driven).
- Fallback chain defined per model family; fallback candidates must be validated for API compatibility.
- Circuit-breaker: after N consecutive errors or SLO breaches for a route, auto-failover to fallback for T minutes.

4) Observability and telemetry:
- Produce metrics: per-route latency histogram, per-model token counts, per-request cost estimate tag, error codes, cache-hit ratio.
- Tracing: propagate x-redwood-trace header; integrate with existing tracing backends (Honeycomb/Jaeger).
- Log retention and sampling strategy defined in infra standards doc.

5) Console UX notes:
- Recommendations panel (left) with prioritized actions: enable KV cache, reduce model size, enable int8 quantization draft.
- Per-route charting with latency/cost overlays and filter by time window.

Configs and thresholds (example table):
| config_key | default | rationale | owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| default_p95_slo_ms_small | 250 | Target P95 for small models | eng-serving-runtime |
| default_p95_slo_ms_large | 600 | Target P95 for large models | eng-serving-runtime |
| batch_max_tokens | 1024 | Upper bound for batching to limit latency | eng-serving-runtime |
| cache_prefix_ttl_sec | 300 | Default TTL for prefix/KV cache entries | eng-platform |

Roadmap & Themes (next 12 months):
- Theme: Performance & Cost Optimization (Q2-Q3 2026)
  - Q2: Baseline benchmarking suite release; automatic batching heuristics.
  - Q3: Kernel selection per-model path + improved quantization profiles.
- Theme: Enterprise Readiness (Q3-Q4 2026)
  - Q3: Dedicated reservation UX and pricing tiers; SLA definitions.
  - Q4: Private deployment hardened installer and KMS integration.
- Theme: Developer Experience & Observability (Q2-Q4 2026)
  - Q2: Console recommendations and per-route cost visualization.
  - Q4: Rollouts with automatic regression detection (prompt-set based).

Milestones and dates (tentative):
1. 2026-04-15: MVP API contracts finalized, schema validated.
2. 2026-05-30: Internal E2E test and load-run for unified-api.
3. 2026-07-15: Beta release to early access customers (limited).
4. 2026-09-01: GA for Hosted API unified features + Redwood Optimize v2.
5. 2026-11-15: Dedicated reservations and SLA publication.

Dependencies and risks:
- Dependency: GPU kernel upstream improvements from runtime team (risk: delayed kernel merges).
- Dependency: Billing/product analytics work to support per-token cost attribution (risk: data model mismatch).
- Risk: Regression in model quality when applying quantization profiles - mitigate with built-in evals and staged rollouts.

Pricing & Packaging notes:
- Pricing principles:
  - Transparent unit economics: surface per-token execution cost and estimate total request cost.
  - Tiers for usage and commitment: pay-as-you-go (hosted), reserved (Dedicated monthly/annual commit), enterprise (Private + platform fee + support).
  - Add-ons: extended observability retention, compliance package, premium SLA.

- Suggested tier matrix (example):
| Tier | Ideal customer | Billing model | Included |
|---|---|---|---|
| Self-serve Hosted | Startups / dev teams | PAYG per token + infra surcharge | API access, Console, 30-day logs |
| Dedicated Standard | Mid-market teams | Monthly reserved capacity | Dedicated GPU pool, 7d logs, baseline SLAs |
| Dedicated Enterprise | High-scale | Annual reserved + volume discount | Higher throughput, 90d logs, SLA 99.9%, support |
| Private | Regulated customers | License + infra + support | Private control plane, on-prem option, KMS/HSM |

- Pricing examples (indicative):
  - Hosted small models: $0.0006 / token (generation) base, dynamic per-model modifier.
  - Embeddings: $0.0002 / embedding unit.
  - Dedicated: committed monthly GPU pool pricing with tiered discounts (custom quotes for >$50k/month).

- Packaging & Flow:
  - Self-serve sign-up -> free credits -> quickstart templates -> usage-to-reservation nudges at $1k/mo threshold.
  - Solutions-assisted onboarding for Dedicated/Private with technical integration and QBR.

Release Notes (candidate release 2026-09-01 GA):
- New: Unified API endpoints for generate, chat, embeddings, and rerank with consistent params and streaming.
- New: Model catalog with per-variant perf profiles surfaced in Console.
- New: Routing policy engine with region and SLO predicates and fallback chains.
- New: Console recommendations (Redwood Optimize v2) to reduce cost and improve latency.
- Improvement: Default batching heuristics reduce average per-token latency by 10% on benchmark workloads.
- Known issues: Int8 quantization recommendations are beta and may cause quality regressions for specific model families. Use per-route QA before global rollout.

Migration and rollout steps (for customers):
1. Sign-up for beta and create a staging route with routing_hint="beta".
2. Run smoke tests and perf benchmarks with customer prompt-sets.
3. Enable Console recommendations and apply changes in staging.
4. Run A/B rollout with 10% traffic for 48 hours, monitoring P95 latency and quality evals.
5. Ramp to 100% if targets met; otherwise rollback and open triage ticket.

Support & escalation:
- First-line: Developer Support (support@redwood.com) - triage and runbooks.
- Escalation: eng-platform oncall -> eng-serving-runtime oncall -> eskalation to Eng SRE manager for cross-team incidents.

Ownership and contacts:

- Technical lead: Marcus Liu (Eng: serving-runtime)

Open questions for review:
- Approve default SLO values or require customer-specific SLOs at onboarding?
- Pricing anchors for Hosted small-model tokens - feedback from finance on market comps needed.
- Scope for early GA vs. beta features (which should remain gated by feature flags).

Appendix: Short CLI examples:
- Generate (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/unified-7b","max_tokens":128,"temperature":0.0}'

- SDK streaming snippet (pseudo):
  client.generateStream({ model: 'redwood/unified-7b', max_tokens: 256 })
    .on('data', chunk => console.log(chunk))
    .on('end', () => console.log('done'))
